concepts.learning_objective: State Kepler's law of orbits and locate the Sun relative to a planet's elliptical orbit.
Relate Kepler's law of areas to conservation of angular momentum under a central force.
Use T^2 proportional to a^3 to compare the periods of planets or satellites.

topics.title: Universal law of gravitation and the gravitational constant

concepts.learning_objective: Apply Newton's law F = G m1 m2 / r^2 to find the force between two masses.
State the force exerted by a uniform spherical shell on a point mass outside and inside it.
Describe how G was measured by Cavendish and state its value and SI unit.

topics.title: Acceleration due to gravity of the earth

concepts.learning_objective: Express g at the earth's surface as G M_E / R_E^2 and use it to compare g on different bodies.
Use g, R_E and G to determine the mass of the earth.

topics.title: Acceleration due to gravity below and above the surface

concepts.learning_objective: Find the variation of g with height above the earth's surface, exactly and for h much less than R_E.
Find the variation of g with depth below the earth's surface using g(d) = g(1 - d/R_E).
Calculate the gravitational potential energy of a system of masses with zero at infinity.
Define gravitational potential as potential energy per unit mass.
Explain mgh as an approximation to the change in gravitational potential energy for small heights.
Derive and use the escape speed v_e = sqrt(2 g R_E) = sqrt(2 G M_E / R_E).
Apply energy conservation to bodies launched at or above escape speed and explain why the moon has no atmosphere.
Find the orbital speed and period of a satellite in a circular orbit around the earth.
Find the kinetic, potential and total energy of an orbiting satellite and explain weightlessness.
